article.title: SurrealDB 3.3 Lets Any Postgres Client Connect and Streams Query Results, but Does Not Speak ANSI SQL
article.summary: SurrealDB 3.3 adds a Postgres wire-protocol listener, row-by-row result streaming and 15 security fixes, though the docs say it speaks SurrealQL, not ANSI SQL.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

SurrealDB 3.3 is out, and its headline feature is compatibility at the connection layer. According to the [SurrealDB 3.3 release notes](https://surrealdb.com/releases/3.3), "any Postgres client or driver, including `psql`, JDBC, npgsql and tokio-postgres, can now connect to SurrealDB." The [protocol documentation](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/rest-api/postgres-protocol) adds an important caveat: "The name 'Postgres protocol' describes the transport layer, not the query dialect."

## What We Know

**Postgres wire protocol.** Per the [protocol documentation](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/rest-api/postgres-protocol), the listener supports simple and extended query flows, prepared statements, interactive transactions, TLS, query cancellation and SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication, and it is switched on with the `--postgres-bind` flag. The [release notes](https://surrealdb.com/releases/3.3) say that "DEFINE USER now stores a SCRAM verifier alongside the password hash." Clients speak SurrealQL by default, with an optional ISO GQL dialect, according to the [documentation](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/rest-api/postgres-protocol).

**Documented limits.** The [documentation](https://surrealdb.com/docs/reference/rest-api/postgres-protocol) lists no ANSI SQL translation, no `pg_catalog` emulation (so schema browsers and some GUI tools will not work), no `LIVE` queries, no `COPY`, and no GQL inside `BEGIN`...`COMMIT` blocks.

**Streaming results.** The [release notes](https://surrealdb.com/releases/3.3) state: "Query results now stream to the client row by row instead of arriving as one buffered response."

**Graph and index performance.** According to the [release notes](https://surrealdb.com/releases/3.3), "Graph adjacency is now stored in compact blocks," and "traversals over high-degree vertices and from many starting records run substantially faster." The same page says that a query filtering on several indexed fields "reads only the records that match all," and that "indexed writes run 2.3 to 2.6 times faster" for full-text indexes. Those are the vendor's own figures; no independent benchmark is cited.

**Transactions and access control.** The [release notes](https://surrealdb.com/releases/3.3) describe locked reads: "`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` registers the records it reads for conflict detection." They also add that "`DEFINE ACCESS ... AUDIENCE` rejects a JWT whose `aud` claim names a different service."

**Storage and search.** File buckets can live in AWS S3 and S3-compatible stores, Google Cloud Storage or Azure Blob Storage, per the [release notes](https://surrealdb.com/releases/3.3), which also add support for Chinese, Japanese and Korean full-text search.

**Security fixes and breaking changes.** The [release notes](https://surrealdb.com/releases/3.3) list 15 security advisories addressed in this release for v3.2.4 and earlier, including a critical cross-tenant access issue. Breaking changes listed on the same page include ISO GQL being enabled by default, a reversed UPDATE/UPSERT evaluation order, and a changed DEFINE MODULE syntax.

## What We Don't Know

- How the Postgres listener performs under real workloads, or how well common drivers and ORMs behave when they expect ANSI SQL; neither source provides testing data.
- Whether the performance gains hold outside the vendor's own scenarios.

## Analysis

The Postgres listener lowers the cost of connecting existing tooling, since drivers and `psql` work as transports. The documented lack of ANSI SQL and `pg_catalog` support, however, means applications written for Postgres queries would still need to be rewritten in SurrealQL or GQL. For operators, the [release notes](https://surrealdb.com/releases/3.3) say "A 3.2 datastore upgrades in place" and that "3.3.0 applies its data migrations automatically on first start," but also that "3.2 and 3.3.0 nodes do not fully interoperate," which matters for rolling upgrades.
